claims.claim: A financial-product recommender can be represented as a sequential decision problem only after states, actions, rewards, transitions, and available information are specified.
claims.limits: This formalism does not prove that the chosen state is Markov-sufficient or that an RL policy is preferable.

claims.claim: Offline evaluation is central when online experimentation is costly or unsafe, but logged-data methods require explicit support, behavior-policy, model, and stationarity assumptions.
claims.limits: No inspected source establishes that the available finance logs satisfy these assumptions.

sources.anchor: Jiang and Li, Sections 3-4 and Theorem 1
Thomas and Brunskill, Sections 4-5 and Appendix J

claims.claim: Naively applying off-policy value learning to a fixed batch can fail because learned policies choose state-action regions poorly represented in the data.
claims.limits: BCQ and CQL benchmark evidence is not finance-domain validation.

claims.claim: Constraint-aware RL methods can encode cost constraints, but a constrained-MDP algorithm does not by itself establish financial regulation, fairness, suitability, or consumer-protection compliance.
claims.limits: The inspected experiments are simulated control tasks, not financial products.

sources.anchor: Achiam et al., Section 3, Propositions 1-2, Algorithm 1, Section 8

claims.claim: The inspected direct credit-card study optimizes whether to increase an existing card's credit limit; it does not choose which product or card to recommend.
claims.limits: The reported policy comparison is simulator-based and synthetic, not live causal deployment evidence.

sources.anchor: Alfonso and Sanchez, Sections 4-6 and Section 8

claims.claim: The inspected CRM study applies deep Q-learning to direct-marketing actions and CLV approximation, but its policy-alignment analysis does not establish causal policy improvement.
claims.limits: The study uses KDD Cup 1998 mailing data and reports final evaluation on the full data set; it is not financial-product recommendation evidence.

claims.claim: The metadata campaign nominates widely cited generic RL-recommender papers and one direct finance-title paper, but metadata alone does not establish technical relevance or correctness.
claims.limits: Citation counts are mutable OpenAlex observations dated 2026-07-21 and all selected seed sources remain locally blocked.

claims.limits: No verified impact-factor values were supplied.

claims.limits: Forward snowballing was not run after the campaign budget was exhausted.

claims.claim: RL improves financial-product recommendation relative to contextual bandits or non-RL recommenders.
claims.limits: No domain-matched comparative experiment with uncertainty support was inspected.
